I have farmed this small plot behind our compound for many years, and with only 0.06 hectares, my grown children and I can manage all the work ourselves without paying for hired labor. The rains here in the South East come well and steady, so I do not need irrigation, and I will spread the compost and goat manure we keep behind the house to feed the soil rather than buying costly chemical fertilizer that is hard to find in the market. I will plant the local cassava and yam cuttings I saved from last season because they fill my family’s belly and I know how they grow here, and I will pull the weeds by hand as I have always done without spraying any chemicals on the crops.
